subject: TTFT & streaming MAP — Finova
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Jared Mills <jared@finova.com>, Priya Shah <pshah@finova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — TTFT & streaming MAP (recap + asks)

Thanks for the time today — good conversation. I wanted to capture the call highlights, open questions, and proposed mutual action plan (MAP) so we have clear owners and timelines. High-level takeaways:

- Goal: Production streaming integration for Finova's conversational assistant by Q3. Key non-functional targets below.
- TTFT target: median <= 120ms for single-turn prompts; P95 goal <= 250ms when under expected concurrency.
- Throughput/peak: baseline 120 req/s, burst capacity up to 300 req/s.
- Concurrency: expected steady 500 concurrent users, design for 800 concurrency headroom.
- Streaming: prefer SSE for browser clients; WebSocket fallback for mobile where persistent connections exist. Chunk cadence: initial packet + follow-up chunks ~200-300ms spacing typical, but can tune in pilot.

Open questions (please confirm):
1) Is Finova able to run a ~2-week mini pilot with a synthetic workload and a small test tenant? (We recommend starting with replayed traffic at target RPS.)
2) Any hard constraints on persistent connections from your infra/security team that would block WS?
3) Acceptance criteria for TTFT (exact metric definitions, sample prompts, and test harness).

Proposed MAP (owners + dates):
- This week: Exchange probe spec + sample prompt set (Markus / Aditya) — target: 2026-05-27
- Next week: Tech kickoff + env prep for mini pilot (Finova infra + Redwood ops) — target: 2026-06-01
- Mini pilot window: 2026-06-07 to 2026-06-20 (traffic replay + live toggled) — target: sign-off by 2026-06-25

Attachments: ttft-ops-questions.xlsx (basic probe matrix & prompts).

Next steps from my side: Aditya will follow up with the technical probe spec and recommended chunking defaults. Soojin will coordinate the pilot runbook and infra checklist. Please confirm MAP dates and call out any procurement or security gating items we should route early.

Thanks,

Markus Klein

Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 09:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery — TTFT & streaming MAP (recap + asks)

Markus — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming a few items from our side:

- The business is comfortable with the TTFT median target of 120ms; procurement will want to see pilot SLOs and billing/overage guardrails before committing to a reserved capacity deal.
- We can run a mini pilot but need a short procurement addendum (2-week trial w/ limited data retention) — I’ll coordinate with finance.
- Regarding streaming: browser clients are preferred via SSE; mobile teams will likely request WS where full-duplex is necessary. We do not have infra-level restrictions on WS, but security will want to review the persistent connection patterns and any connection timeouts.

Two clarifications:
1) For the chunk cadence you mentioned, do you recommend keeping a fixed cadence (e.g., chunks every 250ms) or adaptive cadence tied to model token bursts?
2) For concurrency numbers: our initial traffic spike estimate was 600 concurrent users (internal dashboards) — happy to start with your 800 headroom assumption for safety.

I’ll flag procurement and security review timelines in the MAP once I have internal alignment. Happy to do the Tech kickoff on 2026-06-01 — morning US PT works for our team.

—Jared
Jared Mills

Subject: Re: Discovery — TTFT & streaming MAP (recap + asks)

Quick technical notes to help answer your cadence question and set pilot probes: 

- Recommendation on chunk cadence: prefer adaptive cadence based on token emission, with a soft floor of 150ms between chunks and a soft ceiling of 400ms. This avoids spamming small packets while keeping TTFT low. For UI, send initial chunk (first non-empty payload) asap and then pace.
- Probe harness we’ll deliver will include:
  - 50 synthetic prompts (mix short/long) that map to your primary flows
  - 30-minute steady-state run at baseline RPS (120 req/s)
  - Burst window tests (300 req/s for 5 minutes)
  - Concurrency ramp to 800 with latency histograms collected per second

Fallbacks and graceful degradation:
- If SSE connections hit infrastructure limits, we can route new sessions to a lower-cost non-streaming endpoint with slightly higher TTFT but deterministic payloads (useful as emergency fallback).
- For WS, recommend session heartbeats and per-connection limits; we’ll include recommended timeout defaults in the runbook.

Attachment: I’m attaching a short probe spec and a minimal runbook draft (ttft-probe-spec.md).

Would anyone from Finova’s infra/security be on the call 2026-06-01? If so, send names and we’ll include a short packet on connection patterns for review.

Thanks,
